home.h1: GIF Splitter — Split GIFs into PNG Frames
home.lede: Save one moment or the complete frame sequence.
home.description: Use this GIF frame extractor to turn an animated GIF into individual PNG images. Preview every frame, choose the images you need, and download one PNG or a numbered ZIP. Your GIF and exported images stay on your device.

how.label: From motion to still images
how.title: How to use the GIF splitter
how.intro: A GIF is a sequence of still images with instructions for how long each frame should appear. Splitting it lets you choose a clear tutorial thumbnail, save a reaction image, or inspect a change in an animation. Start with the original GIF file so the tool can read the frames it actually contains.

steps.title: Choose a GIF to split
steps.text: Drop a GIF onto the tool or choose one from your device. Open one file at a time, up to 30 MB and 1,000 frames. Extraction runs in your browser, and the progress indicator shows how many frames are ready. If you only want to explore the controls, try the sample GIF before opening your own file.

steps.title: Preview and select frames
steps.text: Play the animation to locate the scene you want, then use the arrows or slider to compare nearby frames. Click a thumbnail for a larger preview. The frame number and recorded delay help you keep track of your place. Tick checkboxes to select images for a ZIP; use Show more frames to reveal additional thumbnails in a long sequence.

steps.title: Download PNG frames
steps.text: Download this frame saves the image currently in the preview. Download selected creates a ZIP of checked frames, while Download all frames includes the full sequence. The PNGs keep their original frame numbers, so a partial selection still shows where each image came from. Extract the ZIP with your device's file manager before opening the individual PNGs in another editor.

features.title: Full PNG frames at the original dimensions
features.description: GIF splitting should give you images that make sense on their own. Each export represents the complete visible frame at the GIF's original canvas size, whether you save a single moment or a batch.

items.title: Complete images from partial updates
items.text: Many GIFs store only a small rectangle of changed pixels for the next frame. Saving that rectangle alone would leave part of the image missing. The splitter combines these updates and follows the GIF's instructions for retaining, clearing, or restoring earlier pixels. This produces a full image of each animation step rather than a collection of isolated patches.

items.title: PNG output with transparency
items.text: Transparent areas remain transparent in the exported PNG. The checkerboard in the preview helps distinguish them from white or dark pixels and is not included in the download. PNG compression preserves the decoded pixels without introducing another loss of image quality. It cannot recover colors or detail that were already missing from the source GIF.

items.title: Local processing without a watermark
items.text: Your browser reads the selected GIF, reconstructs the frames, and prepares PNG or ZIP downloads on your device. The tool leaves the original file unchanged and adds no watermark. You can open a different GIF after saving your images. Keep any downloads you want before leaving the page, because the current extraction is held in browser memory.

faq.label: Good to know
faq.title: GIF splitter FAQ
faq.intro: Answers about extracting one image, preserving frames, handling larger GIFs, and downloading on a phone.

items.q: How do I split a GIF into frames?
items.a: Choose a GIF from your device and wait for the frame list to appear. The results show the number of frames, canvas dimensions, and recorded duration. Download all frames gives you a ZIP of numbered PNG images in their original order. For a tutorial or reference sheet, check only the frames that show the steps you need and download that selection.

items.q: Does this GIF splitter create shorter animated GIFs?
items.a: This tool separates a GIF into static PNG frames. It does not trim the animation into shorter GIF clips, divide it into animated tiles, or create a new animated file. A ZIP contains separate images; opening it does not play the animation. To rebuild or edit the sequence, extract the PNGs and use another animation editor. You can inspect each frame's recorded delay here, but PNG downloads do not store animation timing.

items.q: Can I extract a single frame from a GIF?
items.a: Yes. Preview the moment you want, then choose Download this frame to save one PNG without downloading the whole animation. Clicking a thumbnail changes the preview; its checkbox controls whether it belongs in a selected ZIP. To save several images together, check their boxes and choose Download selected. Filenames retain the original frame numbers, helping you match downloaded images to their positions in the source.

items.q: Will PNG frames keep their quality and transparency?
items.a: The GIF frame extractor exports the decoded image at the original GIF canvas dimensions, without resizing it to the thumbnail or preview area. PNG uses lossless compression, so exporting does not introduce further compression loss, and transparent areas remain transparent. A GIF may already have a limited color palette or reduced detail; converting it to PNG cannot reverse those changes. The result is a static image of the reconstructed frame, with no preview checkerboard or added watermark.

items.q: Does the GIF splitter upload my files?
items.a: No. Your selected GIF, its filename, and extracted images are processed locally rather than sent to a conversion server. PNG encoding and ZIP creation also happen in your browser. The optional sample downloads a GIF from this website. Loading the site still involves hosting requests, and the production website uses analytics for visits and interactions. The privacy policy explains those services separately from local file processing. Downloads are saved wherever your browser or device normally stores them.

items.q: Is the GIF splitter free, and what are its limits?
items.a: It is free, with no account or added watermark. Open one GIF at a time, up to 30 MB and 1,000 frames. Pixel and memory safeguards may reject an animation below 30 MB: hundreds of full images can take much more space once decoded. Each ZIP supports up to 128 MB of PNG data. If a download exceeds that limit, select fewer frames and save smaller batches. If extraction itself fails on size or memory limits, try a shorter GIF or a version with smaller dimensions.

items.q: Why can some split frames look identical?
items.a: An animation can repeat an image, change only a small area, or use similar frames with different display delays. Exported PNGs contain complete visible frames, including retained pixels, so consecutive images may look identical. Compare the larger preview and check each delay before choosing images to keep. The splitter preserves the source sequence without removing repeated frames. For preview playback, delays below 20 milliseconds are played at 100 milliseconds; the displayed delay remains the value recorded in the GIF.

items.q: Can I split a GIF on my phone?
items.a: Yes. Use a current browser with JavaScript enabled, choose a GIF from your device, and download a PNG or ZIP. The browser's file picker controls which folders or image sources you can access. Open ZIP downloads with your device's Files app or an archive utility. Large animations need more memory, especially on a phone. If you see a size or memory error, use a shorter or smaller GIF. Keep the page open until extraction and the download are finished.

guide.h1: How to split a GIF into frames
guide.intro: Splitting a GIF into frames gives you the individual still images behind the animation. Follow these steps to choose one frame, save a selection or export the full sequence as PNG files with GIF Splitter.

sections.heading: 1. Open the original GIF
paragraphs: Choose a GIF from your device or drag it onto the tool. If you saved it from another website, check that it is actually a GIF: a video renamed with a .gif extension will not decode. The file is read locally and is not uploaded.

The original animation usually gives the most useful result. A screenshot contains only one moment, and a static GIF contains only one frame. The extractor cannot reconstruct motion that is not present in the file.

sections.heading: 2. Find the still image you want
paragraphs: When extraction finishes, the page shows the frame count, original dimensions and recorded duration. Use the arrows or slider to inspect adjacent frames. Click a thumbnail to view it at a larger size; its delay appears in milliseconds.

Play the preview to understand how the frames fit together, then pause on the scene you want. Extremely short delays below 20 milliseconds are played at 100 milliseconds for a usable preview. The displayed timing remains the value stored in the GIF.

sections.heading: 3. Download one PNG or a sequence
paragraphs: Download the current frame to save a single PNG. This is useful for a tutorial thumbnail, an animation reference or a still from a reaction GIF. The downloaded image is static and retains the original GIF canvas dimensions.

For several images, tick their checkboxes and download the selection. Download all frames creates a ZIP of the complete sequence. Filenames use the original frame numbers, including when only selected frames are saved. Extract the ZIP with your operating system or archive app before editing its PNGs.

sections.heading: Why complete frames matter
paragraphs: GIF files often store a small changed rectangle instead of a full image for every frame. They also specify whether earlier pixels should remain, be cleared, or be restored before the next frame. Simply saving those rectangles can produce broken images.

This tool combines the patches and applies these disposal instructions before exporting each PNG. Transparent areas remain transparent; the preview's checkerboard is not baked into the file. Lossless PNG output preserves the decoded pixels, but cannot restore detail missing from the source.

sections.heading: Handling large or damaged GIFs
paragraphs: The input limit is 30 MB and 1,000 frames. A compressed file can expand into many full-size images, so pixel and memory limits also apply. For a very large GIF, try a shorter or smaller source, especially on a phone.

Each ZIP is limited to 128 MB of PNG data. If a full download exceeds that limit, select smaller groups. You can cancel extraction and choose another file. If a GIF is reported as damaged, obtain a fresh copy of the original rather than changing its file extension.

guide.ctaText: Open your GIF, inspect its frames and save a PNG or a numbered ZIP.

about.intro: GIF Splitter turns an animated GIF into useful still images. It is designed for choosing one moment, inspecting an animation or saving its entire frame sequence.

sections.heading: What you can do
paragraphs: Open a local GIF, view each decoded frame and its timing, and save a single PNG. You can also select a few frames or download the complete sequence in a ZIP. Exported images use the original canvas size, with no added watermark.

The tool rebuilds full frames from the GIF's partial image updates. This makes the PNGs suitable for reviewing animation steps, selecting reference images or preparing assets for another editor. Use files you have permission to work with.

sections.heading: Why processing stays local
paragraphs: GIF decoding, PNG encoding and ZIP creation run on your device. No account or file-upload service is required, and your original GIF is not modified. Available memory and device performance affect the animations your browser can handle.

Files are limited to 30 MB and 1,000 frames, with additional decoded-pixel safeguards. Each ZIP is limited to 128 MB of PNG data. A small compressed GIF can still require substantial memory when expanded.

sections.heading: A clear set of capabilities
paragraphs: This site accepts GIFs and produces PNG images or ZIP archives. It does not edit frames, extract video, or build a new animation. PNG export cannot recover detail that was already missing from the GIF.
The guide explains frame timing, transparency and downloads. The privacy page describes local file handling, Cloudflare hosting and the use of Microsoft Clarity for website interaction analytics.

contact.heading: Contact the website operator
paragraphs: GIF Splitter is the name used to operate this tool at www.gifsplitter.com. You can contact the website operator using the email below to report an error, suggest a feature or ask a privacy question.

You do not need to send your GIF or private files to report a problem. A short description, your browser and device type, and any error message are usually enough. Leave out personal information unrelated to your request.

about.ctaText: No account or installation is needed. Choose a file to get started.

privacy.eyebrow: Your files stay on your device
privacy.intro: This policy explains how GIF Splitter handles files and information associated with visiting and using the website. It applies to the tool and its language versions.

sections.heading: GIFs and exported images
paragraphs: Your selected GIF is read by your browser. Decoding, frame previews, PNG encoding and ZIP creation take place on your device. The tool does not upload your GIF, its frames or its filename to a server.

The application keeps working data in browser memory and does not save your GIFs in cookies, local storage or a remote account. Choosing another GIF or closing the page releases the application's current working state. Files you download remain in the location managed by your browser or operating system.

sections.heading: Website hosting
paragraphs: Cloudflare hosts this website and serves its pages, scripts and images. Loading those resources involves routine connection information, such as your IP address, request time, requested URL and browser headers. Cloudflare may process this information in access or security logs according to its own practices.
Choosing the optional sample downloads a sample GIF from this website. It does not send your own files anywhere. The tool does not contact an external conversion or translation service.

sections.heading: Analytics, cookies and local files
paragraphs: Microsoft Clarity loads by default on www.gifsplitter.com to measure page interactions through usage analytics, heatmaps and session replay. It sends interaction and browser data to Microsoft and may set or read cookies depending on Clarity settings, applicable consent signals and browser restrictions. It is not loaded on local or pages.dev previews.

GIF decoding and exports remain on your device. The extraction area, including filenames, previews and extracted frames, is configured for masking in Clarity. The site has no account system and does not store a language preference: the URL determines the language. Microsoft privacy statement: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement

sections.heading: Cloudflare Web Analytics and performance
paragraphs: The production site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics, including a real user monitoring (RUM) beacon, to measure visits and page loading performance. It reports information such as page paths, referring sites, browser and device types, and loading times in website statistics.

Cloudflare Web Analytics does not use cookies or local storage, and does not fingerprint individual visitors. It does not receive your selected GIF or extracted images. These measurements are separate from hosting connection logs and Microsoft Clarity.

sections.heading: Google advertising: current and future use
paragraphs: The site currently does not load Google AdSense advertising code or display Google ads. If Google ads are enabled in the future, Google and its advertising partners may place or read cookies, use web beacons, and process IP addresses and browser or device identifiers to deliver and measure ads, prevent fraud, and personalize ads where enabled and permitted.

Before enabling ads, we will update the policy and provide any required notices and controls for the implemented advertising services. Google's explanation of data use on partner sites: https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites. Google advertising preferences: https://myadcenter.google.com/. These Google controls do not manage Cloudflare or Microsoft Clarity.

sections.heading: Messages you send us
paragraphs: If you email the website operator, your sender address and the message content you choose to provide are processed to handle and reply to your request. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards incoming contact messages to the receiving mailbox. This email flow is separate from the GIF tool, which does not upload files.

Mail providers involved in delivery may process addressing information, message content and attachments. Send only information needed for your request and avoid confidential files. You can use the contact address on the About page for questions about this policy or your information.

sections.heading: Your controls and policy updates
paragraphs: You can use the tool without providing personal profile information. To remove downloaded files, use your device's file manager. Switching language navigates to another page and does not transfer the current GIF to that page.

If the site's data handling changes, this policy will be updated. The date shown here identifies the latest revision. About and the guide provide further information about the tool's capabilities and limitations.

privacy.ctaText: Your browser does the processing. Your GIF stays with you.
